sub_indicators.label: Technical standards for government systems
sub_indicators.subject: gov.standards
sub_indicators.text: National interoperability standards: technical standards for government systems
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Union's Digital Transformation Strategy asks for technical standards, built on open standards, for checking identity in dealings between government, business and citizens. Its interoperability framework names international ones.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the government has no technical standards for its systems to exchange data and none are being written.

Standards are being written: a named set of technical standards for government systems to exchange data is being drafted or is out for consultation. An unapproved edition counts here. A mandate or a stated intention to write standards does not.

Standards are published: the government, the agency responsible or the standards body has issued the data formats, codes, interfaces or protocols its systems must use. An interoperability framework counts only where a source says it sets technical standards. Standards for one sector or one function do not count.

Public bodies are required to use the standards: a law, decree, regulation or circular makes them compulsory for the systems public bodies build or buy. A text that says of itself that it is compulsory does not count.

A system has been checked against the standards in the past three years: a dated source names a public body, system or product tested, audited or certified against them, or gives a count. How good the standards are is not judged.
